draft.title: The excretory system
card: Excretion is the removal of wastes made by the cells of the body. Wastes build up and can harm the body if they are not removed.
two organs that filter the blood. They take out wastes and extra water to make urine.
a stretchy bag that stores urine. Urine leaves the body through a tube when the bladder is emptied.
The skin removes water and some wastes in sweat. The lungs remove carbon dioxide when we breathe out.
draft.remember: Kidneys filter the blood to make urine, the bladder stores it, and skin and lungs also remove wastes.

a.q: Which organ filters wastes from the blood to make urine?
a.why: The kidneys filter the blood and take out wastes and extra water, which form urine. The bladder is the most tempting wrong answer, but it only stores urine after it has been made.
a.clue: Which organ does the filtering, not the storing?

b.q: Sam runs hard on a hot day in Parkes. Which pair of body parts removes wastes as he sweats and breathes out?
b.why: Sweat from the skin removes water and some wastes, and the lungs remove carbon dioxide when he breathes out. The kidneys and bladder deal with urine, so they do not remove wastes through sweat or breath.
b.clue: Think of sweat and of breathing out.

wants.brief: A simple labelled diagram of the human excretory system showing the two kidneys, the tubes leading down, the bladder and the tube that carries urine out of the body.
wants.why: Seeing where the kidneys and bladder sit helps students link each organ to its job.
